title: Armstrong's embouchure and changed attack
summary: Briggs rejects the story that Armstrong shifted embouchures and says his attack turned from precise, as on Cornet Chop Suey, to a push from weak lips.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, now, somebody embouchures told me that he had three different armatures, that he'd move it over to here, and he'd move it over to here, and he'd move it over to here, and around there. Do you believe that?
No, I don't believe that. I believe that he played just that -- that's the only armature embouchure that I saw.
Right. He wasn't moving around at the time.
No, 'cause he -- while we were at Bouchevalles, sometimes he would take up his horn, and try to do something, you know, for me and in my presence, and I never noticed any --
Well, was he losing some range off the top then, or did his tone change?
Yes. He had a very precise attack before, if you listen to "Cornet Chop Suey,".
And recently, when -- I mean, towards the end, it was a push, and not an attack.
Yeh, sure, that's the difference. That's the cause, and that comes from weak lips.
Right. So then he was -- they were just really running him around and working him to death?
Working him to death. That's what they did. They worked him to death. They worked him to death and he was an old man -- well, he recuperated
